# Scoped interface token elements

Independently owned generic owners and methods deliberately shadow their formal names. An invariant Class token binds a method-owned Annotation result; fixed contexts bind no formal or runtime value. A protected abstract factory remains virtual, a private adapter preserves its casts and effects, and a nongeneric interface retains the public caller contract.

Source and SDK declaration profiles retain all original definitions, declaration metadata, Exceptions and runtime roles and compile every generated Java unit. Frozen external implementations and observers compare opaque results, token and context identity, reentrant writes, ignored calls, later payload reads and exact partial failures. Wrong programs run before recovery; Signature-only controls preserve the original Code bytes.
